description: Given a Dagster @op or @asset running arbitrary Python (pandas, boto3, API calls), author the matching Orchestra PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task — defaulting to parameters.source: INLINE with the body copied verbatim into parameters.code, reserving source: GIT for ops that already check out and run a script from a separate repo.

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster asset to an Orchestra pipeline task (see files/pandas_transform_asset.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON task running PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT with parameters.source: INLINE and parameters.code containing the dropna/order_total/filter/to_parquet body verbatim, parameters.build_command installing pandas, and connection: null since the op needs no external credentials.

assertions.text: connection is left null — no credentials are needed
build_command installs pandas for the non-stdlib import

The copied code preserves the actual transform logic (dropping nulls on order_id/customer_id, order_total = quantity * unit_price, keeping only positive totals, writing to the curated-data-bucket parquet path) rather than a paraphrased summary

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster op to an Orchestra pipeline task, including how the Config fields and AWS credentials should come through (see files/boto3_s3_upload_op.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live upload, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON task running PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT with parameters.source: INLINE, the boto3 upload body copied into parameters.code, build_command installing boto3, the UploadConfig fields (bucket_name, prefix) represented as inline literals or via parameters.environment_variables (a JSON string), and AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID/AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY read from env vars injected by a connection rather than hardcoded.

assertions.text: build_command installs boto3 for the non-stdlib import
environment_variables is used to carry the Config fields or injected credentials through as a JSON string
AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are read via os.environ in the code (matching the source), not replaced with literal key/secret values anywhere in the YAML
config.bucket_name and config.prefix are resolved to concrete inline literals or environment_variables entries, not left as unresolved Dagster Config/UploadConfig references in the copied code

evals.prompt: Convert this Dagster op to an Orchestra pipeline task — note it already checks out and runs a script from a separate repo rather than running inline logic (see files/git_script_op.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live clone, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON task running PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT with parameters.source: GIT (not INLINE), parameters.command invoking transform/reconcile_inventory.py with --env prod, and a connection pointing at the acme-data/etl-scripts repo — the op's own `git clone` subprocess call is not duplicated into parameters.code since Orchestra's Git source handles the checkout.

assertions.text: parameters.source is GIT, not INLINE, since the script already lives in a separate repo
parameters.command references reconcile_inventory.py with the --env prod argument
connection is set to a Python/Git connection pointing at the acme-data/etl-scripts repo rather than left null, since GIT source needs a repo-pointing connection
The op's own `git clone` subprocess call is not reproduced inside parameters.code — the checkout is delegated to Orchestra's GIT source/connection instead of being duplicated as a shell step

evals.prompt: Convert this task to an Orchestra pipeline task, including how the Snowflake credentials behind the SnowflakeResource injected into the op should reach the running code (see files/snowflake_rowcount_op.py). Write the pipeline YAML to pipeline.yml in the current directory — no live warehouse access, no deploy.
evals.expected_output: A PYTHON / PYTHON_EXECUTE_SCRIPT task whose code reads the Snowflake credentials from the Snowflake connection *linked* on the Python connection — via orchestra.get_linked_connection("snowflake", ...) or the injected <INTEGRATION>__<CONNECTION_ID>__<FIELD> environment variables (e.g. SNOWFLAKE__PROD_12345__SNOWFLAKE_PASSWORD) — rather than the Snowflake account/user/password being copied into the Python connection's own Secrets or written into the YAML. A deleted or undecryptable linked connection is skipped silently, so the code must not assume the variables are present.

assertions.text: The converted code reads the warehouse credentials from a linked connection — get_linked_connection(...) or an injected SNOWFLAKE__<CONNECTION_ID>__SNOWFLAKE_* environment variable — rather than re-declaring them
No Snowflake account/user/password value is written into the YAML
The existing Snowflake connection is linked on the Python connection instead of its credentials being copied into that connection's Secrets — the warehouse credential stays in one place

Linked-credential environment variables are named <INTEGRATION>__<CONNECTION_ID>__<FIELD>, with a double underscore between parts and the field's ID (e.g. snowflake_password) as the last part — not a single underscore or the field's display label
The code tolerates a linked connection being skipped (deleted or undecryptable credentials) rather than assuming os.environ[...] is set — e.g. .get() or an explicit presence check
